student_notes: Questions from production engineer review. Focus on practical application.

questions.question: An A/B experiment has traffic_pct=10 and two variants (50/50 split). Session 'abc123' is assigned. On turn 3, session 'abc123' makes a new request. Which variant does it get?
options: A. It might get a different variant — assignment is turn-level, not session-level
B. The same variant as before — assignment uses hash(session_id + experiment_id) % 100 which is deterministic
C. It re-evaluates based on current traffic_pct, which may have changed since turn 1
D. It always gets the control variant after turn 2
questions.explanation: hash(session_id + experiment_id) % 100 is a deterministic, session-level assignment. The same session_id always hashes to the same number, so the same variant is selected regardless of turn count or when the request arrives. This is critical for experiment validity: showing a user Haiku on turn 1 and Sonnet on turn 3 would produce confounded measurements. The experiment framework stores experiment_id and experiment_variant in state for every turn so they're emitted to Kafka even if the variant doesn't change.
